scores.evidence: Critical path: historical data access (M0) → replay/backtest (T11–T12) → S2 go/no-go → model v1 → shadow validation (M2) → model validation → enforcement (M4).
scores.rationale: Milestones and tasks build substrate (infra, schemas, velocity) before policy, replay, model and enforcement, with explicit dependencies and rules enforced before the model.

scores.evidence: the Decision Service runs in staging, answering the Auth Service's sandbox calls in shadow mode. It writes decision records to the data lake
scores.rationale: M1 is a real end-to-end thin slice (API→Redis→Kafka→lake) with CI/CD and deploy, though in staging rather than prod; prod shadow follows in M2, which is nearly but not fully prod.

scores.evidence: D9 ... Off-ramp at the end of M1 ... Revisit if: The S2 spike shows < ~10% value-detection lift
scores.rationale: Ten decisions with options, reversibility and revisit triggers, plus assumptions with impact and validation dates and defaults for open questions.

scores.evidence: Rules (M3) go before the model (M4); Rollback levers, fastest first; T5 skeleton → T6, T8, T9 in parallel
scores.rationale: Widest-impact items (contract, infra, schemas, API skeleton) precede leaf work, and rollout goes rules before model, by small percentage steps.

scores.evidence: Timing: PCI scoping doc and QSA review in M1 (T19). Controls in M2.
scores.rationale: M1 has mTLS/HMAC, token-only schema and scoping, but security is largely a standalone section, with pen test and controls later, so not concretely threaded in every phase.

scores.evidence: Observability (M1 baseline, full set in M2)
scores.rationale: T16 provides an M1 baseline with alerts, and later phases add dashboards and the anomaly alert, but it is mostly described in a standalone section and the M3/M4 treatment is thin.

scores.evidence: Terraform staging ... destroy + recreate succeeds; image to ECR tagged with git SHA; a second run gives byte-identical decisions
scores.rationale: IaC, SHA-tagged images, versioned immutable snapshots and models, deterministic replay, and golden vectors are present from M1 onward.

scores.evidence: Failure and degradation ladder ... during a Kafka outage, API p99 stays unchanged and drops are counted
scores.rationale: Degradation, circuit breaker, deadline fallback and fault-injection are built in M1, with restore drill in M2 and game day/kill switches in M3.

scores.evidence: No LLMs. ... evaluation comes first, in M1; Promotion gates; shadow challenger; kill switch per model (→ rules-only)
scores.rationale: Classical ML with eval, HITL approvals, fallbacks and rollout guards before enforcement, but no explicit layered AI order or budgets; the retrieval→memory→orchestration stack is largely N/A.

scores.evidence: Deferred | Trigger to build ... Merchant/device/IP velocity ... Card-testing across many cards at one merchant shows up in losses
scores.rationale: Explicit deferred table with triggers, non-goals, per-milestone exclusions and shortcut payback conditions.

note: Strong, well-sequenced plan with a thin-slice M1, explicit decisions, and deferrals; weaker on security and observability being threaded through all phases, and the AI-layer ordering is only partially applicable.
